title: Import service: text, number and date parsing behaviour, review notes
context: Review notes written by the engineer who maintains the supplier-file import service, for the team lead and QA, ahead of adding two new supplier formats. Each statement is meant to be backed by the snippets in the appendix; most were run locally and the terminal output pasted.

claims.text: The import job processes about 50,000 rows per minute.
On Python 3.12, len('\u0130'.lower()) is 2.
int(' 7 ') raises ValueError because of the surrounding spaces.
'MX-USD-02'.removeprefix('MX-') and 'MX-USD-02'.lstrip('MX-') both give 'USD-02', so removeprefix and lstrip are interchangeable for any code that starts with 'MX-'.
parse_import_date() accepts dates written as DD/MM/YYYY.
parse('ABC-123 x4') returns ('ABC-123', 4), and parse matches SKUs regardless of letter case.
For 'straße' and 'STRASSE', a.casefold() == b.casefold() is True while a.lower() == b.lower() is False.
len('e\u0301') is 1, the same as the composed character.
first() and the Row type alias work on any Python from 3.10 onward.
iso_week_start() returns the Monday of the ISO week for the scheduler.
(date(2025, 3, 1) - date(2025, 2, 1)).days is 28, so adding timedelta(days=28) to any date lands in the following calendar month.
Splitting raw on commas and stripping each part gives ['SKU-001', 'SKU-002', 'SKU-003'], dropping the empty field.
parse('ABC-123  x10 extra') returns None because of the trailing text.
parse_csv_line() keeps commas that appear inside quoted fields.
date(2024, 2, 29).replace(year=2025) returns 28 February 2025.
json.dumps({'amount': Decimal('1.10')}) raises TypeError unless default=str is passed.
json.dumps({'b': 1, 'a': 2}, sort_keys=True) returns '{"a": 2, "b": 1}', so json.dumps produces identical text for any two equal dicts.
'SKU-KUS'.strip('SKU') returns '-KUS'.
'MX-MXN-01'.lstrip('MX-') returns 'N-01', because lstrip removes characters rather than a prefix.
'a  b'.split(' ') returns ['a', 'b'].
date(2024, 12, 30).isocalendar() is (2025, 1, 1), so 30 December 2024 belongs to ISO week 1 of 2025.
parse() runs on Python 3.7 and every later release.
'42'.isdigit() and '٤٢'.isdigit() are True and int() parses both, so whenever s.isdigit() is True, int(s) succeeds.
json.loads('{"a": 1, "a": 2}') keeps the first value and returns {'a': 1}.
int('٤٢') returns 42: int() accepts Arabic-Indic digits.
On Python 3.10, json.dumps('ñ') also returns an ASCII-escaped string.
date(2024, 1, 31) + timedelta(days=30) is 2 March 2024.
For every code in S2, removeprefix('MX-') keeps the currency code intact: 'MXN-01', 'USD-02' and 'MXN-03'.
normalise_phone() strips the +52 country prefix.
Spreadsheets dropped into the import folder are decoded as cp1252.

Python 3.14.5
$ cat snippet.py
import re

PATTERN = re.compile(r"(?P<sku>[A-Z]{3}-\d{3})\s+x(?P<qty>\d+)")


def parse(line):
    if (m := PATTERN.search(line)) is None:
        return None
    return m["sku"], int(m["qty"])


for line in ["ABC-123 x4", "abc-123 x4", "ABC-123  x10 extra", "ABC-12 x1", "ref ABC-1234 x2"]:
    print(f"parse({line!r}) -> {parse(line)!r}")
$ python3 snippet.py
parse('ABC-123 x4') -> ('ABC-123', 4)
parse('abc-123 x4') -> None
parse('ABC-123  x10 extra') -> ('ABC-123', 10)
parse('ABC-12 x1') -> None
parse('ref ABC-1234 x2') -> None
